Abdur Razzaq, Advocate -----For the Accused- Petitioner.

Ali Ahsan Mujahid ----- Accused-Petitioner 
Vs.
State ----- Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
2. This is an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for anticipatory bail of the accused-petitioner Mr Ali Ahsan Mujahid, an ex-Minister-in-Charge of the Ministry of Social Welfare, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in connection with Shahbag PS Case No. 53 dated 26-2-2008 under sections 409/406/109/419/420 of the Penal Code, 1860 read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 5. It has been also alleged in the first information report that the accused-petitioner being one of the Members of the Cabinet Purchase Committee abetted the offence and thereby committed criminal misconduct punishable under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 7.  Mr Abdur Razzaq further submits that the informant of the case being an officer of the Anti-Corruption Commission acted malafide in lodging the first information report with the concerned Police Station against the petitioner in view of the fact that one Dr Sadat Hossain, the then Cabinet Secretary (now Chairman of Bangladesh Public Service Commission) being a Member of the Cabinet Purchase Committee was not named in the first information report as an accused, albeit he played a crucial role in awarding the contract to the CMC Consortium and the non-mentioning of the name of Dr Sadat Hossain as an accused in the first information report is indicative of malafides on the part of the-Anti-Corruption Commission and the Commission has adopted a pick-and-choose policy in launching the prosecution against the accused petitioner along with others. 

 10. In a last-ditch attempt, Mr Abdur Razzaq submits that on 2-6-2008 one Dr Taslima Ahmed Zaman, daughter of Mr Tofail Ahmed, an ex-Minister, was granted ad interim pre-arrest bail on the ground of malice in law, by this Bench in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7809 of 2008 and, as such, the accused-petitioner standing on the same footing with her may be granted the same relief and this ground has been taken in the supplementary affidavit filed today by the accused-petitioner. 

 11. Per contra, with the leave of the Court, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission, submits that it is an indubitable fact that the first information report was lodged with the concerned police station against the accused petitioner and others on 26-2-2008 and since then several months have elapsed by now; but the law enforcing agency, or for that matter, the police have not attempted to hunt him down, rather after the initiation of the case, the Investigating Officer quizzed him and recorded his statement under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and this being the scenario, no occasion has arisen to seek pre-arrest bail by the accused-petitioner. 

 12. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan next submits that regard being had to the ratio decidendi by our Appellate Division in the case of the State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury reported in 51 DLR (AD) 242, the accused-petitioner cannot maintain this application for anticipatory bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before this Division and, as such, it should be rejected in limine. 

 13. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan further submits that in view of the embargo imposed by Rule 19Gha of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007, the bail application of the accused-petitioner is not entertainable, though a door has been opened by the Appellate Division in the unreported decision in the case of the State vs Moyezuddin Sikder rendered in Criminal Appeal No. 65 of 2007. 

 14. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan also submits that it is true that Dr Sadat Hossain was a Member of the Cabinet Purchase Committee and undeniably he is not a first information report named accused; but nonetheless, the criminal law has been set in motion by way of lodgment of the first information report with the police station and during investigation of the case, necessary incriminating materials, if any, will be collected and thereafter a police report will be submitted and in the police report, Dr Sadat Hossain mayor may not be sent up depending on his prima facie complicity or otherwise in the commission of the offence and, such being the position, it cannot be said at this stage that the Anti-Corruption Commission has adopted a pick-and choose policy in launching the prosecution against the accused-petitioner. 

 17. However, according to Mr Abdur Razzaq, the accused-petitioner has been roped in the case for political victimisation and harassment out of bad faith. It is also the assertion of Mr Abdur Razzaq that the accused-petitioner has surrendered before the High Court Division personally for pre-arrest bail under compelling circumstances and apprehending that he will not get a fair deal from the lower Court because of interestedness and over-enthusiasm of the Anti-Corruption Commission, in particular. Anyway, assuming for the sake of argument that the accused-petitioner has the legal standing to make an application for pre-arrest bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as mandated by the Appellate Division in the case of the State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury reported in 51 DLR (AD) 242, we have no option but to hold that during the currency of the Proclamation of Emergency, the Emergency Power Rules of 2007 holds the field in respect of the offences specified in the Schedule of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. Sections 409 and 109 of the Penal Code, 1860 and the offences punishable by the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, amongst others, have been incorporated in the Schedule of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act. So it is easily understandable that Rule 19Gha of the Emergency Power Rules will come into play in soft as this case is concerned. 

 18. In this context, we feel tempted to refer to the relevant findings of our Appellate Division in the case of the State vs Moyezuddin Sikder made in Criminal Appeal No. 65 of 2007 for the purpose of disposal of the instant application which are quoted below verbatim: 

 (2) The High Court Division misdirected itself in entertaining the objection to the bar under Rule 19Gha of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 and in embarking upon deciding the issue as a general proposition divorced from the facts of the casein view of the principle that 'general propositions do not decide concrete cases. 

 (3) Regardless of the ouster. of the jurisdiction, there may be cases depending On the facts of each case making out a case of without jurisdiction, coram non-judice or malafide arid finding of the Court to that effect upon final adjudication and determination and then in those cases, the bar in Rule 19Gha in granting bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure will not apply. 

 19. By the way, it may be mentioned that there may be other cases wherein the bar slapped by Rule 19 Gha of the Emergency Power Rules will not apply as held in the case of the State vs Moyezuddin Sikder adverted to above. 

 20. The Appellate Division has also held in that case the expression 'Adalat or Tribunal' in Rule 19 Gha includes the Supreme Court of Bangladesh so far the bar in granting bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is concerned. 

 21. Coming back to the present case before us, the question of malafides has been alleged in launching the prosecution against the accused-petitioner regardless of the ouster of the jurisdiction of the Court or Tribunal as envisaged by Rule 19Gha. It goes without saying that the proviso to Rule 19Gha will not be applicable so far it relates to the accused-petitioner. Although the question of without jurisdiction or coram non-judice has been asserted by the accused-petitioner in initiating the proceedings against him, but even prima facie there are no materials on record to that effect. 

 23. Be that as it may, Dr Taslima Ahmed Zaman was granted ad-interim anticipatory bail on 2-6-2008 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7809 of 2008 mainly by invoking the proviso to Rule 19Gha of the Emergency Power Rules and in view of the allegation of apparent malice in law in that no notice was served upon her in accordance with Rule 15Gha of the Emergency Power Rules. But in the instant case, to all intents and purposes, malice in fact has been alleged which cannot be inferred instantly because of the fact that it rests upon evidence and trial. 

 24. There is no gainsaying the fact that Dr Sadat Hossain is not a first information report named accused. But, nevertheless, after investigation of the case, he may or may not be sent up in the police report on the basis of his prima facie complicity or otherwise in the commission of the alleged offence. At the moment, we are unable to hold that the Anti-Corruption Commission has adopted a pick-and-choose policy in launching the prosecution against the accused-petitioner. On this point, we are at on with Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan. 

 25. The unreported decision of the Appellate Division in Criminal Appeal No. 65 of 2007 has thrown light upon the interpretation of some of the provisions of the Emergency Power Rules and the grounds on which an accused may pray for bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. From a plain reading of Rule 19Gha and the unreported decision of our Appellate Division in Criminal Appeal No. 65 of 2007, it leaves no room for doubt that the filing of an application for bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been hemmed in except in the cases elucidated in the said decision. It appears that the accused-petitioner does not fall within the ambit of those cases. So, it necessarily follows that the embargo imposed by Rule 19Gha of the Emergency Power Rules comes into play insofar as the accused petitioner is concerned. Apart from the ouster of the jurisdiction as contemplated by Rule 19Gha and as held by the Appellate Division in Criminal Appeal No. 65 of 2007, the allegation of mala fides, as raised by Mr Abdur Razzaq, we feel constrained to opine, can only be gone into at the time of final adjudication and determination of the matter. In other words, the allegation of malafides in launching the prosecution against the accused-petitioner cannot be readily accepted or inferred and there must be a positive finding as to malafides upon final adjudication and determination as held by our Appellate Division in Criminal Appeal No. 65 of 2007. 

 26. From the foregoing discussions and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, we are led to hold that at this stage, the accused-petitioner cannot make any application for bail, far less anticipatory bail, under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. Accordingly, the instant application for anticipatory bail is summarily turned down.
